script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: "The Misadventures of Mildred and Marty"

FADE IN:

INT. MILDRED'S APARTMENT - DAY

*MILDRED, a quirky, forty-something woman with a penchant for eccentric fashion, is hunched over a steaming bowl of oatmeal, her laptop open on the table.*

MILDRED
(Muttering to herself)
This is it, Mildred. Today is the day.

*Her phone rings. She jumps, spilling a drop of oatmeal on her sleeve.*

MILDRED
(Excited)
Hello?

MRS. LEE
(Voice from the phone)
Mildred, dear, I'm so glad I caught you. I need your help.

*Mildred's expression sours as she recognizes the voice of her disapproving neighbor.*

MILDRED
(Sighing)
What now, Mrs. Lee?

EXT. APARTMENT BUILDING - DAY

*Mildred and MRS. LEE, a prim, proper older woman, stand in the sunlit courtyard, their voices carrying through the open windows of the surrounding apartments.*

MRS. LEE
Mildred, your parrot, Marty, is creating quite a disturbance. I've received several complaints.

MILDRED
(Frustrated)
What can I do about it? He's just being a parrot.

MRS. LEE
You could try to train him to be quieter. I know a man who specializes in bird training.

INT. MILDRED'S APARTMENT - DAY

*Mildred sits at her laptop, staring at an open email from a bird trainer named MARTIN. She hesitates, then clicks the "Reply" button.*

MILDRED
(Typing)
Hello, Martin. I'd be happy to bring Marty in for training. When can you come?

EXT. MILDRED'S APARTMENT - LATER

*Martin, a friendly, middle-aged man with a soft spot for birds, arrives with a large, brightly-colored cage. Mildred greets him warily as he sets up the cage in her living room.*

MARTIN
(Smiling)
Don't worry, Mildred. I'll have Marty behaving himself in no time.

INT. MILDRED'S APARTMENT - LATER

*Mildred and Martin sit on the couch, watching as Marty squawks and flaps inside the cage. Mildred rolls her eyes.*

MILDRED
(Sarcastically)
He's really making progress.

MARTIN
(Grinning)
Give him time, Mildred. And maybe a little more attention.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

*Mildred sits at a table, her laptop open in front of her, typing away. Marty is perched on her shoulder, preening his feathers. A young woman, LUCY, approaches.*

LUCY
(Excitedly)
Oh, look! It's that cute parrot!

MILDRED
(Smiling)
Why, thank you. This is Marty.

LUCY
(Sitting down across from Mildred)
I've always loved parrots. They're so colorful and lively.

MILDRED
(Nodding)
Yes, they have their moments.

LUCY
(Curious)
So, what do you do, Mildred?

MILDRED
(Pausing)
I'm a writer.

LUCY
(Surprised)
Really? What do you write?

MILDRED
(Shrugging)
A little of everything. Short stories, poetry, screenplays.

LUCY
(Eyes widening)
Screenplays? That's amazing! I've always wanted to write one.

INT. MILDRED'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

*Mildred sits at her laptop, staring at a blank screen. Marty is perched on the back of her chair, watching her with bright, curious eyes.*

MILDRED
(Whispering to herself)
I can't do this. I don't have what it takes to write a successful screenplay.

MARTIN
(Appearing behind her)
You do have what it takes, Mildred. You just need to believe in yourself.

MILDRED
(Startled)
Martin? How did you get in here?

MARTIN
(Grinning)
I've been listening to you, Mildred. I saw how discouraged you were. I wanted to offer you some encouragement.

MILDRED
(Softly)
Thank you, Martin. I needed that.

EXT. APARTMENT BUILDING - DAY

*Mildred and Martin sit on the courtyard bench, watching as children play in the sunshine. Marty perches on Mildred's shoulder, preening his feathers.*

MILDRED
(Smiling)
You know, Martin, maybe I'll try writing a screenplay about a quirky, forty-something woman who learns to believe in herself.

MARTIN
(Laughing)
I'd love to read that one, Mildred.

FADE OUT.

---

THE END
